items.stem: What did Benjamin "Pap" Singleton organize after Reconstruction ended?
items.stemEs: ¿Qué organizó Benjamin "Pap" Singleton después del fin de la Reconstrucción?

choices.text: A legal challenge to segregated railroad cars in Louisiana
choices.textEs: Una demanda judicial contra los vagones de ferrocarril segregados en Luisiana
choices.explanation: That challenge was mounted in New Orleans and reached the Supreme Court as Plessy v. Ferguson in 1896. It was a real effort of the same era by other people, and it was fought in the courts rather than by moving anyone.
choices.misconception: attributes a separate legal campaign in Louisiana to Singleton

choices.text: Black migration out of the South to colonies in Kansas
choices.textEs: La migración de personas negras del Sur hacia colonias en Kansas

choices.text: Emigration to Liberia under the American Colonization Society
choices.textEs: La emigración a Liberia bajo la Sociedad Americana de Colonización
choices.explanation: Liberian emigration was a real and competing answer to the same conditions — the ship Azor carried migrants from Charleston in 1878 — but it was a different organisation with a destination across an ocean. Singleton's colonies were in Kansas.
choices.misconception: merges two emigration movements of the same years and sends the Exodusters to Liberia

choices.text: Testimony to a Senate committee investigating the exodus
choices.textEs: Testimonio ante un comité del Senado que investigaba el éxodo
choices.explanation: Singleton did testify before a Senate select committee in 1880, so this is true. The question asks what he ORGANISED, and answering a summons is not organising a migration.
choices.misconception: answers with something true about Singleton that is not the thing he organised

items.dokRationale: The student retrieves what Singleton is known for. No relationship between facts has to be worked out, so recognising the Kansas migration is recall.
items.explanation: Singleton was born enslaved in Nashville and spent the late 1870s persuading Black Tennesseans and Deep South families to leave for Kansas, where he helped settle colonies. He called himself the Moses of the Colored Exodus, and the migrants who followed became known as Exodusters.
items.explanationEs: Singleton nació esclavizado en Nashville y dedicó los últimos años de la década de 1870 a persuadir a familias negras de Tennessee y del Sur profundo de marcharse a Kansas, donde ayudó a establecer colonias. Se llamaba a sí mismo el Moisés del Éxodo de Color, y los migrantes que lo siguieron pasaron a conocerse como Exodusters.

items.stem: Why did the Exodusters leave the South for Kansas in 1879?
items.stemEs: ¿Por qué los Exodusters abandonaron el Sur para ir a Kansas en 1879?

choices.text: The Homestead Act offered public land to any citizen willing to farm it
choices.textEs: La Ley de Asentamientos Rurales ofrecía tierras públicas a cualquier ciudadano dispuesto a cultivarlas
choices.explanation: The Act of 1862 was real and it did draw migrants toward Kansas. But it is a reason to choose that destination, not a reason to abandon the South, and the question asks why they left.
choices.misconception: answers with what drew them to Kansas rather than what drove them out of the South

choices.text: Northern factories were recruiting Black workers for wartime jobs
choices.textEs: Las fábricas del Norte reclutaban trabajadores negros para empleos de guerra
choices.explanation: That recruitment belongs to the Great Migration after 1916, roughly forty years later. In 1879 the destination was farmland in Kansas, not factory work in Northern cities.
choices.misconception: places the Great Migration's factory recruitment in 1879

choices.text: With Reconstruction over, they had no protection from violence or debt
choices.textEs: Terminada la Reconstrucción, no tenían protección frente a la violencia ni frente a las deudas

choices.text: Southern planters encouraged the migration to reduce competition for land
choices.textEs: Los hacendados del Sur fomentaron la migración para reducir la competencia por la tierra
choices.explanation: Planters worked to stop the exodus, not to speed it: they needed the labour, and they blocked river landings and threatened families who tried to leave. The direction of the pressure is the opposite of this.
choices.misconception: reverses the planters' stance, treating those who obstructed the exodus as its sponsors

items.dokRationale: The student has to separate a push from a pull — why people left, as against what made one destination attractive. Naming Kansas would be recall; sorting the causes is a relationship.
items.explanation: The exodus followed the collapse of Reconstruction government. Once federal backing was gone, Black Southerners faced violence with no prospect of prosecution and worked land under contracts and debts they could not escape. Kansas was a destination; the conditions they were leaving are what made so many take it.
items.explanationEs: El éxodo siguió al derrumbe de los gobiernos de la Reconstrucción. Una vez perdido el respaldo federal, los sureños negros enfrentaban la violencia sin posibilidad de que hubiera procesamientos y trabajaban la tierra bajo contratos y deudas de los que no podían librarse. Kansas era un destino; las condiciones de las que huían son lo que llevó a tantos a tomarlo.
items.tcapFormatReason: not affirmed — no human has judged this item field-testable

items.stem: How did Benjamin "Pap" Singleton reach the families he hoped would move to Kansas?
items.stemEs: ¿Cómo llegaba Benjamin "Pap" Singleton a las familias que esperaba que se mudaran a Kansas?

choices.text: He testified before a Senate select committee about the exodus
choices.textEs: Testificó ante un comité selecto del Senado sobre el éxodo
choices.explanation: He did, in 1880, after the migration was well under way. Explaining a movement to senators is not how he reached the families who joined it.
choices.misconception: answers with a true later act rather than with how he recruited

choices.text: He recruited through circulars distributed by the Freedmen's Bureau
choices.textEs: Reclutaba mediante circulares distribuidas por la Oficina de Libertos
choices.explanation: The Freedmen's Bureau had been shut down by 1872, years before the exodus. Singleton worked through an association he helped form in Nashville, not through a federal agency that no longer existed.
choices.misconception: keeps the Freedmen's Bureau operating into the exodus years

choices.text: He founded the colony at Nicodemus, Kansas
choices.textEs: Fundó la colonia de Nicodemus, en Kansas
choices.explanation: Nicodemus was a real Black settlement in Kansas, founded in 1877 by a different group of promoters. Singleton's own colonies were elsewhere in the state, and founding a town is not how he reached people still in the South.
choices.misconception: credits Singleton with a Kansas colony other promoters founded

choices.text: He printed and circulated handbills advertising Kansas colonies
choices.textEs: Imprimía y distribuía volantes que anunciaban las colonias de Kansas

items.dokRationale: The student has to tell a method of recruitment apart from other true facts about the same man and the same movement. Recalling that he favoured Kansas would be DOK-1; identifying how he reached people requires sorting his activities by purpose.
items.explanation: Singleton helped form a homestead association in Nashville and promoted Kansas with printed circulars passed hand to hand through Black communities. Print was how a man with no office and no newspaper reached families hundreds of miles apart, and it is why the migration spread faster than anyone could organise it from one place.
items.explanationEs: Singleton ayudó a formar una asociación de colonización en Nashville y promovió Kansas con circulares impresas que pasaban de mano en mano por las comunidades negras. La imprenta fue el modo en que un hombre sin cargo ni periódico llegaba a familias separadas por cientos de millas, y por eso la migración se extendió más rápido de lo que nadie podía organizarla desde un solo lugar.
